s:
A solutions architect needs to improve an application that is hosted in the AWS Cloud. The application uses an Amazon Aurora MySQL DB instance that is experiencing overloaded connections. Most of the application's operations insert records into the database. The application currently stores credentials in a text-based configuration file. The solutions architect needs to implement a solution so that the application can handle the current

connection load. The solution must keep the credentials secure and must provide the ability to rotate the credentials automatically on a regular basis. Which solution will meet these requirements?
o: Deploy an Amazon RDS Proxy layer in front of the DB instance. Store the connection credentials as a secret in AWS Secrets Manager.
Deploy an Amazon RDS Proxy layer in front of the DB instance. Store the connection credentials in AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store.
Create an Aurora Replica. Store the connection credentials as a secret in AWS Secrets Manager.
Create an Aurora Replica. Store the connection credentials in AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store.

w.y: The problem is connection overload on a write-heavy workload, so read replicas do not help. RDS Proxy pools and shares database connections. It retrieves credentials from Secrets Manager, which has built-in automatic rotation for Aurora credentials.

o.A: Correct: RDS Proxy pools connections, and Secrets Manager stores and rotates the credentials automatically.
o.B: Parameter Store has no native automatic rotation, and RDS Proxy expects credentials in Secrets Manager.
o.C: Aurora Replicas serve reads only; the insert load still overloads the writer's connections.
o.D: A replica does not fix write connection overload, and Parameter Store has no built-in rotation.

s: Setting up database credentials for RDS Proxy - Amazon Aurora
Set up automatic rotation for Amazon RDS, Amazon Aurora, Amazon Redshift, or Amazon DocumentDB secrets
